question.text: This empire located in the Indian subcontinent was founded by Babur. Shah Jahan who built the Taj Mahal, was a ruler of this empire.
question.clue: In the 18th century, the Bengal War and the Carnatic Wars caused this dynasty to lose territory to France and Great Britain.

swap.leadin: Three prominent figures with this last name were assassinated by political and/or religious opponents inthe twentieth century.
swap.text: Give this shared surname of several figures in Indian political history, including Prime Minister Rajiv andindependence leader Mahatma.
swap.clue: Another leader with this surname resolved some tension with a western neighbor in the 1972 Shimla Agreement and was opposed by the Janata Party.

question.leadin: In a speech after an attack by Nathuram Godse, this politician declared "friends and comrades, the light has gone out of our lives."
question.text: Name this politician, who not even a year earlier gave his inaugural address titled "Tryst with Destiny." This politician was the first prime minister of a newly independent India.
question.clue: During a crisis over Kashmir, this man instructed his defense minister V.K. Menon to undertake an 8-hour filibuster in front of the U.N. Security Council.

swap.text: Rajendra Chola also defeated this island's kingdom of Anuradhapura. Arab merchants monopolized this island's city of Colombo to trade with its Sinhalese kingdoms.
swap.answerHtml: Sri Lanka [or Ceylon; or the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; or Ilangai Jananayaka Socialisa Kudiarasu; or Sri Lanka Prajatantrika Samajavadi Janarajaya]
swap.clue: Ashoka's son Mahinda traveled as a missionary to a king of this location named Devanampiya Tissa.

question.leadin: Violent anti-Sikh riots broke out in India in 1984.
question.text: This operation targeted Sikh secessionists in the Golden Temple. The Indian army has been accused of stealing religious relics during its execution.
question.clue: Following this action, Operation Woodrose purged members of the Akali Dal who had earlier drafted the Anandpur Resolution.

swap.text: The East India Company army was led by this man, who assumed command of the Company army following his unsuccessful bid for a seat in the House of Commons.
swap.clue: The definitive biography of this man is H.H. Dodwell's, which contrasts him to his French counterpart, Joseph Dupleix.

question.leadin: Answer the following about national leaders following successful independence movements.
question.text: Tajuddin Ahmad served as this nation's first Prime Minister after rising to power through his party, the Awami League. It broke away from Pakistan in 1971 to form a new nation with capital Dhaka.
question.clue: A terrorist attack in this country saw five hundred small bombs explode at various government buildings within a span of 30 minutes; that attack was carried out by the JMB.

swap.leadin: This leader's government attempted to implicate labor leader George Fernandes in the Baroda Dynamite Case, but Fernandes successfully ran for Parliament from prison.
swap.text: Name this leader who wielded near-absolute power during a 21-month-long period known as the Emergency. This leader later ordered the controversial Operation Blue Star.
swap.clue: The "Smiling" Buddha nuclear test was conducted under this leader, who ruled through executive decree and suspended civil liberties during a period known as the "Emergency."

question.leadin: In 1962, 15,000 people of Chinese heritage living in this city were sent to prison camps following a border war.
question.text: Name this city whose Christian minority was served by the Missionaries of Charity, a group whose founder won the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize.
question.answerHtml: Kolkata [or Calcutta] (The Missionaries of Charity was founded by Mother Teresa.)
question.clue: Governmental offices from Murshidabad were moved to this city by Warren Hastings.

swap.leadin: Name these nineteenth-century conflicts involving Britain.
swap.text: This 1857 revolt in India was allegedly brought on by the cartridges for the new Enfield rifles being greased with pork and beef fat.
swap.clue: The notoriously bloody Siege of Cawnpore took place during this event, which was triggered by a new Enfield cartridge that used animal fats as grease, thus offending both Hindus and Muslims.

question.text: A sculpture depicting four of these animals, standing back-to-back and representing the four cardinal directions, originally appeared on the top of the Ashoka pillar at Sarnath.
question.clue: Bertel Thorvaldsen's sculpture of one outside Lucerne commemorates the Swiss Guards who died in the French Revolution.

swap.leadin: One of these things in Lumbini described how a ruler visited the city 20 years into his reign and abolished taxes there.
swap.text: Name this collection of over thirty inscriptions that encourage right behavior and kindness towards animals and others. These inscriptions were created in response to the violence of the Kalinga War.
swap.answerHtml: edicts of Ashoka [accept pillar edicts of Ashoka, accept rock edicts of Ashoka, accept pillars of Ashoka, accept pillars of Dharma, prompt on partial answers]
swap.clue: These documents outline a policy of proselytism towards the neighboring king Antiochus I, though they promote tolerance of all religions.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Himalayan Kingdoms.
question.text: The Kingdom of Gorkha would be disestablished by Prithvi Narayan Shah in 1768. That ruler would establish this Kingdom in its place, which would last until the 2001 Royal massacre.
question.clue: Chhetris dominated this kingdom's politics, especially after the Kot Massacre reduced its king to a figurehead.

swap.leadin: A musical automaton of a tiger mauling a European man was discovered in this ruler's capital after its capture by the British.
swap.text: Name this "Tiger of Mysore" who, along with his father, resisted the British East India Company in four wars. His defeat at the Battle of Seringapatam ended Mysore's independence.
swap.clue: The V&A owns a wooden automaton commissioned by this man of a creature biting into the neck of a Western soldier.

question.leadin: The Federal Party led a protest outside the Galle Face Green against a prime minister with this surname.
question.text: Give this surname of Solomon, who was assassinated by a Buddhist monk after he signed a pact with the leader of the Federal Party. The first woman to become a prime minister in Asia had this last name.
question.clue: This family of Chandrika Kumaratunga, or CBK. Her father Solomon, known as the "Silver Bell of Asia," was assassinated by a Buddhist monk in 1959, after which, her mother Sirimavo became the world's first female prime minister as chair of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party.

swap.text: Both Harper and the UK House Foreign Affairs Committee cited the human rights violations of this Sri Lankan president who used heavy-handed tactics to end his country's long-running civil war.
swap.clue: The Tamil Tigers were defeated in 2009 under the leadership of this President of Sri Lanka who suffered a shock defeat in the 2015 presidential election to Maithripala Sirisena.

question.text: Ibrahim Nasir won this country's independence from Britain, then formed an undemocratic People's Majlis ("MAJ-leese"). The United Suvadive Republic seceded from this country, which reelected, then re-abolished, its Dhivehi sultanate.
question.answerHtml: Maldives [or Republic of Maldives; accept Maldive Islands or Sultanate of Maldives]
question.clue: In the 20th century, this country was long led by the dictator Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who sparked civil unrest in 2005 by arresting the main opposition figure, Mohamed Nasheed.

swap.leadin: This sultanate was usurped by the Hindu banker Raja Ganesha, who made a deal with Muslim nobles that his son would convert to Islam and succeed him as Jalal al-Din.
swap.text: Name this sultanate founded by Ilyas Shah, who moved the capital to Pandua and remained largely independent of Delhi. This late medieval sultanate expanded the trade of its lands' renowned muslin.

question.text: The death of Queen Tripurasundari and the adulthood of a king of this name led to Bhimsen Thapa's fall from power and suicide. A king of this name succeeded his father Raja Raja as second king of the Chola kingdom.
question.clue: A ruler with this regnal name, his empire's last, died in Pazhayarai in 1279 after submitting to Jatavarman Sundara.

swap.leadin: This engagement pitted some turmeric-smeared forces on one side and Najib Khan's excellent defensive formations on the other.
swap.text: Name this 1761 battle in which the light Afghan cavalry led by Ahmad Durrani were finally able to overcome French-trained artillery commanded by Sadashivrao Bhau.
swap.clue: The offensive that led to this battle began when one side crossed the Jumna River and cut off their opponents' supply lines, forcing them to fight or starve.
